mainTopic: The rules of ערובי תבשילין (size and דעת), and making ערובי חצרות on a יום טוב that falls on Friday
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: in the הרסנא dish, the flour is the main part. רבי אבא then rules that an ערובי תבשילין must be at least a כזית, and one כזית works for one person or a hundred. Two sources that seem to allow less are read so they fit this rule. Next, רב says an ערובי תבשילין needs דעת. The גמרא shows from great רבנים who made one ערוב for a whole city that the people it covers do not need to know about it, as long as they are within the תחום שבת. A story about שמואל and a blind man shows that someone who keeps forgetting may not rely on another's ערוב. The גמרא then turns to a יום טוב on Friday: the תנא קמא forbids ערובי תחומין and ערובי חצרות, while רבי allows ערובי חצרות. רב and שמואל argue over the הלכה, and the גמרא tries to prove from a story whether ruling like רבי is lenient or strict. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The flour is the main part of the fish dish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion: in the הרסנא dish, the flour, not the fish fat, is the main part.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought the fish fat is the main part. The ruling teaches us that the flour is the main part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a discussion that started before this section. It says that in the הרסנא dish the flour counts as the main part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought the dish is judged by its fish fat. The ruling teaches that the flour is what counts. That makes the non-Jew's cooking a real, important new dish, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Small fish or fish fat fried with flour

phrases.english: [you might have said] the fish fat is the essential element,
he teaches us that the flour is the essential element.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion from before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In הרסנא the flour is the main part, so the dish counts as a new, important cooked food.

steps.title: An ערוב of cooked food needs a כזית
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that an ערובי תבשילין must be at least the size of an olive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: An ערובי תבשילין needs to be the size of an olive.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אבא sets a minimum size for the food used in an ערובי תבשילין: a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we knew you need a cooked food set aside before יום טוב. רבי אבא adds a size requirement. A tiny crumb is not enough; it must be at least a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Cooked food set aside before יום טוב so one may cook on יום טוב for שבת
The size of an olive, a basic halachic measure

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base rule that everything else in the section tests and protects.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
A joining of cooked foods requires an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The food of an ערובי תבשילין must be at least a כזית.

steps.title: One כזית for everyone, or one for each person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether one כזית is enough for a whole household or whether each person needs a separate כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is one olive-bulk enough for all of them, or does each and every person need an olive-bulk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי אבא's rule. When many people rely on one ערוב, how much food is needed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since an ערוב needs a כזית, maybe the amount grows with the number of people relying on it. The question is whether the כזית is a fixed amount or an amount per person.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
one olive-bulk for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא כְּזַיִת לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד?
phrases.english: or perhaps an olive-bulk for each and every one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי אבא's rule reaches
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the כזית size go up with the number of people relying on the ערוב?

steps.title: One כזית works for one or a hundred
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes רב: one כזית is enough whether the ערוב is for one person or a hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אבא said in the name of רב: An ערובי תבשילין needs an olive-bulk, whether for one person or for a hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רב. A single כזית covers any number of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'whether for one or for a hundred' settle it. The כזית is a fixed amount, not a per-person amount. One ערוב of a כזית serves the whole group.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether for one or for a hundred

steps.whatToRemember: An ערובי תבשילין needs a כזית, and one כזית is enough for any number of people.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Come and hear, that Rabbi Abba said that Rav said:
A joining of cooked foods requires an olive-bulk
whether for one or for a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One כזית is enough no matter how many people rely on it.

steps.title: The משנה says even a tiny leftover is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if any amount of the ערוב is left, one may still rely on it. Does that mean less than a כזית works?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If he ate it or it got lost, he may not start cooking based on it. If he left any amount of it, he may rely on it for שבת. What does 'any amount' mean? Doesn't it mean even less than an olive-bulk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge from the משנה against the כזית rule. The משנה says 'any amount' left is enough, which sounds smaller than a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase כל שהוא usually means even a tiny amount. If a tiny leftover keeps the ערוב valid, then the ערוב does not seem to need a כזית. That would clash with רבי אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even tiny
From the start, as his plan

phrases.english: We learned: If he ate it or it was lost —
he may not cook relying on it from the start,
phrases.notes: 'From the start' means he can't begin cooking for שבת on יום טוב based on this ערוב.

phrases.english: if he left any amount of it —
he may rely on it for Shabbat.
What is 'any amount'?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא כְּזַיִת?
phrases.english: Is it not even though there is not an olive-bulk?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי אבא's כזית rule against the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's rule that an ערוב needs a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'any amount' left is enough, a piece smaller than a כזית must be valid.

steps.title: 'Any amount' still means at least a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a leftover that is still at least a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means there is at least an olive-bulk in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבא by reading the משנה differently. The leftover still has a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any amount' does not mean smaller than a כזית. It means any amount of what remains, as long as at least a כזית is left. So the משנה and רבי אבא fit together.

phrases.english: No, it means that there is an olive-bulk in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Any amount' means even less than a כזית.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Any amount' means any leftover that is still at least a כזית.

steps.title: A teaching says the ערוב has no set size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching that lists foods fit for the ערוב and says it has no size, at the start or the end. Does that mean no minimum at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A cooked dish can be roasted, or even pickled, well-boiled, or regularly cooked. It can even be soft Spanish fish that had hot water poured on it before יום טוב. Both at the start and at the end it has no set size. Doesn't that mean it has no size requirement at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge against the כזית rule. A teaching says the ערוב has no שיעור, which sounds like no minimum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching first lists which kinds of cooked food count. Then it says the ערוב has no size 'at the start or the end'. If that means no limit at all, even a crumb would work, which goes against רבי אבא.

phrases.english: Come and hear: A cooked dish — this is roasted,
and even pickled, well-boiled, or cooked,
and Spanish soft fish

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנָּתַן עָלָיו חַמִּין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: upon which he poured hot water on the eve of the Festival —
its beginning and its end have no measure.
phrases.notes: 'Beginning' is the size when it's first set aside; 'end' is what's left after some is eaten or lost.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, אֵין לוֹ שִׁיעוּר כְּלָל?
phrases.english: What, is it not that it has no measure at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the כזית rule, from a different source
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's rule that an ערוב needs a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'No measure' sounds like no minimum at all, so less than a כזית would be valid.

steps.title: No maximum, but there is a minimum
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'no measure' means there is no upper limit, but there is still a lower limit of a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it has no measure on the upper end, but it does have a measure on the lower end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the כזית rule again. 'No measure' only means there is no maximum size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching never meant a crumb is enough. It means you can use as much food as you like. Still, there is a minimum, the כזית, so רבי אבא's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges fail. An ערובי תבשילין has no maximum size, but it must be at least a כזית, from start to end.
steps.confusionAlert: 'No measure' here does not mean 'any size works.' It only means there is no upper limit.

phrases.english: No, it has no measure upward,
but it has a measure downward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No measure' means no minimum at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No measure' means no maximum; the minimum is still a כזית.

steps.title: An ערובי תבשילין needs דעת
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב: an ערובי תבשילין only works if there is דעת, meaning awareness and intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: An ערובי תבשילין needs awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב: an ערובי תבשילין does not work by itself. Someone has to know about it and mean it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about the size of the food (a כזית). Now the focus moves from the food to the people. The rule says a mental part, דעת, is needed, but it does not yet say whose דעת counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'joining of cooked foods' set aside before יום טוב so one may cook on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
A joining of cooked foods requires awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the size discussion and opens a new topic about the intention needed for the ערוב.

steps.title: Whose awareness is needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the person who sets up the ערוב obviously must know about it. It asks whether the people it is made for must also know.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that we need the awareness of the one who sets it down. Do we also need the awareness of the one it was set down for, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב's rule covers. Does it only mean the person making the ערוב, or also the people who benefit from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setter's דעת is taken for granted, so the real question is about the beneficiary. If the beneficiary must know, one person could not quietly make an ערוב for others who are unaware of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who sets down (the ערוב)

phrases.english: It is obvious that we require the awareness of the one who sets it down;
the awareness of the one for whom it was set down —
do we require it, or do we not require it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רב's rule reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must the beneficiary of the ערובי תבשילין also know about it?

steps.title: Great רבנים made one ערוב for a whole city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings proof: אבוה דשמואל made an ערוב for all of נהרדעא, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי made one for all of טבריה. רבי יעקב בר אידי announced that anyone could rely on his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמואל's father would make an ערוב for all of נהרדעא. רבי אמי and רבי אסי would make an ערוב for all of טבריה. רבי יעקב בר אידי would announce: Whoever did not set down an ערובי תבשילין may come and rely on mine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with real cases. Leaders made one ערוב that covered an entire city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every person in a whole city could have known about the ערוב ahead of time. Since these leaders still made it for everyone, the beneficiary's דעת is apparently not needed. Only the setter has to intend it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practice of a community leader making an ערובי תבשילין for the whole town.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that Shmuel's father
would make an eiruv for all of Neharde'a,
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
would make an eiruv for all of Tiberias.
Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi would announce:
Whoever did not set down a joining of cooked foods,
let him come and rely on mine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל מְעָרֵב אַכּוּלַּהּ נְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with real practice.
steps.raayaObject: The beneficiary's דעת is not required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of אבוה דשמואל, רבי אמי, רבי אסי, and רבי יעקב בר אידי of making one ערוב for a whole city.

steps.title: How far can such an ערוב reach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far away a person can live and still rely on someone else's ערוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to how far?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next step. It asks for the outer limit of who is covered by a city-wide ערוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that one ערוב can cover others, the גמרא needs to know where its coverage ends.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much / how far?

phrases.english: And up to how far?
phrases.notes: He means: how far from the person who made the ערוב can you be and still be covered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the city-wide ערוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distance limit for relying on another person's ערוב.

steps.title: Up to the תחום שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב נחומי בר זכריה, quoting אביי, says one is covered up to the תחום שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחומי בר זכריה said in the name of אביי: Up to the תחום שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the distance question. A person within the תחום שבת of the one who made the ערוב is covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit is the area a person may walk to on שבת and יום טוב. Someone who lives beyond that distance is not included in that ערוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Shabbat boundary, the 2,000-אמה walking limit

phrases.english: Rav Nechumi bar Zecharya said
in the name of Abaye:
Up to the Shabbat boundary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Coverage reaches up to the תחום שבת.

steps.title: שמואל lets a sad blind man rely on his eiruv
steps.stepSummary: A blind man who recited משניות before מר שמואל was sad because he forgot to make an ערובי תבשילין. שמואל told him to rely on his.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a blind man who used to recite משניות before מר שמואל. שמואל saw that he was sad and asked: Why are you sad? He answered: Because I did not set down an ערובי תבשילין. שמואל said: Rely on mine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. It shows a great רב letting someone who forgot rely on his ערוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier steps: one person's ערוב can cover another. The first year sets up the contrast that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Recites teachings in order (a memorizer of teachings)

phrases.english: There was a certain blind man
who would recite teachings in order
before Mar Shmuel.
He saw that he was sad.
He said to him: Why are you sad?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּלָא אוֹתִיבִי עֵרוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין.
phrases.english: He said to him: Because I did not set down a joining of cooked foods.
He said to him: Rely on mine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing a person relying on someone else's ערוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who forgot may rely on another's ערוב.

steps.title: A repeat forgetter is called negligent
steps.stepSummary: The next year the blind man forgot again. שמואל told him he was a פושע: everyone else may rely on his ערוב, but not him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year שמואל saw that he was sad and asked: Why are you sad? He answered: Because I did not set down an ערובי תבשילין. שמואל said: You are negligent. For everyone else it is permitted; for you it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a limit. Someone who keeps forgetting out of carelessness may not rely on another person's ערוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A community ערוב is meant for people who forgot by accident, not for people who lean on it instead of making their own. Since the setter's דעת decides who is included, שמואל could leave out a careless person.
steps.whatToRemember: One person's ערובי תבשילין can cover others, even without their knowledge, if they are within the תחום שבת. It does not cover someone who keeps forgetting out of carelessness.

phrases.english: The next year he saw that he was sad.
He said to him: Why are you sad?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּלָא אוֹתִיבִי עֵרוּבֵי תַּבְשִׁילִין.
phrases.english: He said to him: Because I did not set down a joining of cooked foods.
He said to him: You are negligent.
For everyone else it is permitted,
for you it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: שמואל means his ערוב was never meant to include a person who keeps forgetting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story by adding a limit to relying on another's ערוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who is repeatedly negligent may not rely on someone else's ערובי תבשילין.

steps.title: No ערובי תחומין or ערובי חצרות on a Friday יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when יום טוב falls on ערב שבת, one may not make ערובי תחומין or ערובי חצרות on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: When a יום טוב falls on Friday, one may not make an ערוב, neither an ערוב of boundaries nor an ערוב of courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It covers the other kinds of ערוב that cannot be made on a יום טוב that falls on Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike ערובי תבשילין, which is made before יום טוב, these two kinds of ערוב cannot be set up on the יום טוב itself for the שבת that follows. If someone did not make them before יום טוב, it is too late.

keyTerms.meaning: An ערוב that extends how far one may walk
An ערוב that joins courtyards so one may carry between them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three kinds of ערוב. ערובי תבשילין is about cooking. ערובי תחומין is about walking distance. ערובי חצרות is about carrying between courtyards.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: A Festival that occurs on Shabbat eve —
one may not make an eiruv,
neither a joining of boundaries
nor a joining of courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about other kinds of ערוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת, one may not make ערובי תחומין or ערובי חצרות.

steps.title: רבי allows ערובי חצרות but not ערובי תחומין
steps.stepSummary: רבי disagrees with the תנא קמא and permits ערובי חצרות on a יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת, but not ערובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: On this יום טוב you may make an ערוב for courtyards, but not an ערוב for the תחום שבת. You may restrict a person in something that is already forbidden to him, but not in something that is permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step continues. Now רבי gives a second opinion that splits the two kinds of ערוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbade both kinds of ערוב on this יום טוב. רבי makes a distinction. Walking past the תחום is forbidden on יום טוב too, but carrying between domains is permitted on יום טוב, so the two kinds of ערוב are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: An ערוב that joins courtyards so a person may carry between them on שבת
An ערוב that extends how far a person may walk on שבת
You restrict him or forbid him

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not lenient across the board. He permits only ערובי חצרות. He agrees that ערובי תחומין may not be made on that יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, giving a second opinion in the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: One may make an eiruv for courtyards,
but not an eiruv for Shabbos boundaries.
Because you may restrict him
in a matter that is forbidden to him,
phrases.notes: For example, walking past the תחום, which is forbidden on יום טוב as well.

phrases.english: but you may not restrict him
in a matter that is permitted to him.
phrases.notes: For example, carrying between domains, which is allowed on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the ברייתא quoted in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, ערובי חצרות may be made on a יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת, but ערובי תחומין may not.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about the halacha
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like the תנא קמא, who forbids both kinds of ערוב. שמואל rules like רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רב said the הלכה follows the תנא קמא. שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree about which opinion in the ברייתא is the final halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that no ערוב at all may be made on that יום טוב. שמואל holds like רבי, which seems to allow ערובי חצרות.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
The final ruling follows this opinion

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav said: The halacha follows the first Tanna.
And Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא from steps 16-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב rules like the תנא קמא. שמואל rules like רבי.

steps.title: Is ruling like רבי lenient or strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's ruling 'like רבי' is meant as a קולא or a חומרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: When שמואל says the הלכה follows רבי, does that make things more lenient or more strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about what שמואל's ruling actually means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing whose name שמואל followed is not enough. We need to know whether רבי's position is the lenient one or the strict one.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; a question raised in the בית מדרש

phrases.english: They asked:
"The halacha follows Rabbi"—
is it to be lenient or to be strict?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what שמואל's ruling from step 18 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether following רבי leads to a lenient or a strict result.

steps.title: Obviously it means lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the question is pointless, since רבי clearly permits more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it obvious that he meant it to be lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question it just asked. According to the ברייתא as we have it, רבי is the one who permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא as quoted, the תנא קמא forbids both kinds of ערוב and רבי permits ערובי חצרות. So ruling like רבי should obviously be the lenient side.

phrases.english: It is obvious that he said it to be lenient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the question in step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא presents רבי as the lenient opinion, so there should be nothing to ask.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר reported that the opinions are reversed
steps.stepSummary: The question was needed because רבי אלעזר sent word that the ברייתא should be learned with the opinions switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question arose because רבי אלעזר sent a message to בבל: It is not as you learn it there, that רבי permits and the חכמים forbid. Rather, רבי forbids and the חכמים permit. So what is the ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why its question was a real one. There is another version of the ברייתא in which רבי is the strict one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אלעזר's version is correct, then 'like רבי' would be a חומרא. That makes the question in step 19 a real doubt, and it ends with 'מאי?', meaning: so which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: You learn or recite a text

phrases.english: Because Rabbi Elazar sent a message to the Diaspora:
Not as you learn it in Babylonia,
that Rabbi permits and the Sages forbid;
rather, Rabbi forbids and the Sages permit.
So what is the ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 and restates the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different version of the source text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is clear that רבי is the lenient one.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a version in which רבי is the strict one, so the meaning of שמואל's ruling is in doubt.

steps.title: The story of רב תחליפא בר אבדימי
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא בר אבדימי ruled in practice like שמואל, and רב said that this young scholar's first ruling led to a ruined הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב תחליפא בר אבדימי acted in practice like שמואל, and רב said: The first ruling of this young scholar has led to ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to help settle whether שמואל's ruling was lenient or strict. This step sets up the proof, and the next step draws the conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב strongly disapproved of the ruling made according to שמואל. The way he described it, as a 'ruin', will show which way שמואל ruled.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi
acted in practice like Shmuel,
and Rav said:
The first ruling of this young scholar
is for ruin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּרַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a proof to answer the question in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: Whether שמואל's ruling like רבי is a קולא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב תחליפא בר אבדימי and רב's reaction

steps.title: A ruin only makes sense if the ruling was lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רב's word 'ruin' seems to fit only a lenient ruling, which would show that שמואל ruled like רבי לקולא. The next step pushes back on this proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say שמואל meant it to be lenient, that explains the 'ruin.' But if you say he meant it to be strict, what ruin is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to draw a proof from the story: רב's complaint seems to show that שמואל's ruling was a קולא. The next step challenges this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is that being too strict does not seem to ruin anything, but wrongly permitting something does. If so, רב's word 'ruin' would show that ruling like רבי meant permitting ערובי חצרות. The next step questions this assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say; this explanation works
That is it; this explains it

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tries to prove from רב's word 'ruin' that ruling like רבי is a קולא. The next step pushes back: a strict ruling can also cause 'ruin'.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
he said it to be lenient — that is the ruin.
phrases.notes: A play on words: קולא (leniency) and קלקולא (ruin) sound alike.

phrases.english: But if you say it was to be strict —
what ruin is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the story in step 22.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's description of the ruling as קלקולא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This is only an attempted proof that ruling like רבי is lenient. Step 24 begins to reject it.

steps.title: Even a strict ruling can ruin the masses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the proof from step 23. A חומרא can also be called 'ruin', because it causes the רבים to go wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the masses are ruined by it (by forbidding them to make the עירוב),
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the proof from the last step. This line sets up the answer: if the ruling makes the רבים go wrong, it can be called 'ruin', even if it was strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said the word 'ruin' only fits a lenient ruling. Now the גמרא says a strict ruling can also ruin things. If people are told they cannot make an עירוב חצרות on this יום טוב, they may end up carrying on שבת without one. So the word 'ruin' no longer proves the ruling was לקולא.

keyTerms.meaning: They are ruined; they go wrong
By it, meaning by this ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'ruin' means only that the ruling itself was too lenient. Here the 'ruin' is what happens to people's behavior: a strict ruling can lead the public into mistakes.

phrases.english: Since the masses are ruined by it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the strict ruling: people barred from making the עירוב might carry on שבת anyway. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 23's claim that the word 'ruin' can only describe a lenient ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof drawn from רב's word 'ruin' (קלקולא) that שמואל ruled לקולא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed only a lenient ruling can be called 'ruin'. But a strict ruling that leads the public into mistakes (carrying on שבת without an עירוב) can also be called 'ruin'.
